problem:
For the piecewise function 

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}3{e}^{\,\,sin(x-1)}\, & \text{ for }\,x<1 \\ p{x}^{3}\, & \text{ for }\,x\ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

it is known that ${lim}_{x\to 1}f(x)=3.$ What is the value of the constant $p?$

$p=$
{{field-1}}

feedback.worked_solution:
In order for ${lim}_{x\to 2}f(x)$ to be equal to $8,$ the left and right-sided limits must both exist and be equal to $8.$

- Approaching from the left, we have $x\le 2,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=a{x}^{2}+2x-3.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}(a{x}^{2}+2x-3) \\  & =a({2}^{2})+2(2)-3 \\  & =4a+1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the left-sided limit must be equal to $9,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}f(x) & =9 \\ 4a+1 & =9 \\ 4a & =8 \\ a & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

- Approaching from the right, we have $x>2,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=4x+b.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}(4x+b) \\  & =4(2)+b \\  & =8+b\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the right-sided limit must be equal to $9,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}f(x) & =9 \\ 8+b & =9 \\ b & =9-8 \\ b & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
